reconcile.note: Matthew Henry harmonizes the agents by arguing Yahweh only permitted Satan to incite David, since God himself tempts no one.

discrepancy.note: Strauss traces the swap directly: what Samuel blames on God's anger, the Chronicler reassigns wholesale to the devil.

quotes.text: David’s culpable project of numbering the people, which in the second book of Samuel was traced to the anger of God, is in the later chronicles ( 1 Chron. xxii. 1 ) put directly to the account of the [ 260 ] devil
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), p. 260, on 2 Samuel 24:1 and 1 Chronicles 21:1.

sides.snippet: he moved David against them, saying, Go, number Israel and Judah
sides.verseText: Again the anger of Yahweh was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them, saying, Go, number Israel and Judah.

sides.snippet: Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to number Israel
sides.verseText: Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to number Israel.
